title: Between Floors
cues: Two years I been callin' 'bout the elevator, man
Gray concrete, distant elevator doors, looping digital clock face
build
Two years of "file a ticket," "we'll get to it," "understand"
Stacked paperwork, a red 'file' icon pulsing with faint light
build
Seventh floor, bad knee, and my mama in a chair
A shadowed, worn armchair, a single hand resting on the armrest
build
Every time it broke, I had to carry her the stairs
Silhouetted figure ascending stairs, strained limbs, desperate movement
build
Then a notice on my door, "Thirty days, you're out"
A stark white notice, floating on a dark, textured wall
build
'Cause I called the city twice, and I opened up my mouth
A hand outstretched, a muted mouth forming an 'O' of despair
drive
Mister Pell come by Tuesday with a clipboard and a tie
A dark suit, a clipboard held rigidly, a focused, shadowed face
drive
Showin' off my unit to a man with cash to buy
Golden light reflecting off a stack of bills, a shadowy hand reaching for them
drive
Pressed the button for the lobby, and I stepped in too
A metallic elevator door closing with a pneumatic hiss, a contained space
drive
He said, "Take the stairs," I said, "Sir, I'm comin' through"
A figure standing motionless, a hand raised in a questioning gesture
drive
Doors shut, little jolt, and the light went red
Red emergency lights flashing, a still, darkened elevator shaft
drive
Stopped dead between the fourth floor and the fifth instead
A distorted reflection in a polished metal floor, a sense of entrapment
drive
Between floors, between floors, now you feel it in your chest
A swirling, chaotic vortex of deep blues and purples
drive
Two years of "file a ticket," now you sweatin' through your vest

drive
Between floors, between floors, ain't no up and ain't no down
Multiple shadows merging into a single, suffocating mass
drive
Only way you walkin' out is if we settle it right now
A frantic hand reaching for a button, a sense of impending doom
drive
First hour, he was cool, makin' calls on his phone
A blurred, indistinct figure on a sleek, modern phone
drive
No bars in the shaft, man, you on your own
Darkness within a confined shaft, a solitary, struggling hand
drive
Second hour, tie loose, he was poundin' on the door
Hands pounding aggressively on a metal door, a frustrated silhouette
drive
Third hour, suit off, he was sittin' on the floor
A slumped figure seated on the floor, illuminated by a single, harsh light
drive
I said, "Relax, I been stuck in here eleven times this year
A hand clutching at a wrist, a blurred face in agitation
drive
I know the latch up on the hatch, I know the way from here
A dark, looming latch, a reflective metal surface
drive
But my arms get kinda weak when I'm worried 'bout my lease
A shaky hand hovering over a hatch, a weary expression
drive
And it's hard to lift a hatch when a man can't sleep in peace"
Multiple hands intertwined in a desperate, silent plea
drive
He said, "Name your price," I said, "It ain't a price, it's a list
A stack of documents growing higher, a sense of mounting tension
drive
Fix the box by Friday, and the rent don't move from this
Ink flowing from a pen, a single dark signature on a white surface
drive
Rip the notice into pieces, sign it on the back with me"
A shattered notice, fragments floating in a dim, enclosed space
drive
And his hand was shakin' worse than my mama's on her knee
Shaking hands, blurred and indistinct, a moment of vulnerability
drive
Nine. Hours. In. A. Box.
A single, distorted figure suspended within a black box
drive
You. Own. The. Floors. I. Own. The. Clock.
A grand clock face, frozen at nine, a sense of timeless entrapment
drive
Who's. The. Landlord. Up. Here. Now?
Two mirrored hands reaching towards an empty space
drive
Sign. It. Slow. And. Sign. It. Loud.
A blurred, isolated figure against a stark white backdrop
drive
He signed it on the notice with my pen against the wall
A dark, heavy pen scratching across a white surface, a final signature

Pulled him up into the shaft, and he was cryin' on the cable

Walked him to the fifth-floor doors and pried 'em open where I'm able

A figure seated on a bench, bathed in the glow of a streetlamp
